objects.description: Bitstream ID header for an Ogg Opus stream. Contains core playback parameters (channels, pre-skip, original input sample rate, output gain, mapping family and layout). Used by libopusfile to configure decoding and channel mapping.
Vorbis-style comment header metadata for an Ogg Opus stream. Holds vendor string and a list of (tag,value) comment entries. Binary-compatible with vorbis_comment.
Decoded representation of a METADATA_BLOCK_PICTURE tag: descriptive fields, dimensions, and the embedded image data (or URL), with detected format when recognized.
Information parsed from HTTP/Shoutcast/Icecast response headers for URL streams (e.g., station name, description, content type, nominal bitrate, flags).
Callback vtable used by libopusfile to read/seek/tell/close an abstract byte stream backing an Ogg Opus source.
Opaque handle for an opened Ogg Opus stream managed by libopusfile. Represents decoder state, stream topology (links), buffering, and headers. Full definition is private to the library.

functions.name: opus_head_parse
functions.signature: int opus_head_parse(OpusHead *_head, const unsigned char *_data, size_t _len)
functions.description: Parses an Opus ID header packet into an OpusHead structure. Use to validate and retrieve stream parameters (channels, mapping, gain, etc.). On error, _head is left unchanged. Pass _head = NULL to validate only.
requirements: _data must point to the full ID header packet; _len is its byte length.
_data must begin with the ASCII string "OpusHead" or the function returns OP_ENOTFORMAT.
Channel mapping family 255 is rejected (returns OP_EIMPL) for general-purpose players.
If parsing fails, return is a negative error; check it before using _head.
_head may be NULL to perform validation only.

functions.name: opus_granule_sample
functions.description: Converts an Opus granule position to a 48 kHz sample offset for a given stream. Effectively returns _gp - _head->pre_skip, but safely handles very large (wrapped) granule positions and negative results.
requirements: _head must be a valid, initialized OpusHead for the stream.
Returns -1 if _gp < _head->pre_skip (audio that should not be played).
Counts samples at 48 kHz.

functions.name: opus_tags_parse
functions.signature: int opus_tags_parse(OpusTags *_tags, const unsigned char *_data, size_t _len)
functions.description: Parses an Opus comment (OpusTags) header packet into an OpusTags structure. Use to retrieve vendor string and user comments. On error, _tags is left unchanged. Pass _tags = NULL to validate only.
requirements: _data must point to the full 'OpusTags' header packet; _len is its byte length.
_data must begin with the ASCII string "OpusTags" or the function returns OP_ENOTFORMAT.
If memory allocation fails, returns OP_EFAULT.
On failure, do not use or free fields in _tags.

functions.name: opus_tags_copy
functions.description: Performs a deep copy of an OpusTags structure from _src to _dst.
requirements: _dst must be a valid pointer to an OpusTags to receive the copy.
_src may be NULL only if caller intends undefined behavior; passing NULL violates OP_ARG_NONNULL(1) only on _dst. Source must logically be a valid OpusTags.
On failure (OP_EFAULT), _dst remains unmodified.

functions.name: opus_tags_init
functions.description: Initializes an OpusTags structure for use before adding or parsing tags.
requirements: _tags must be a valid pointer to an allocated OpusTags.
Call before using _tags with add/query functions or before manual population.
After use, free with opus_tags_clear().

functions.name: opus_tags_add
functions.signature: int opus_tags_add(OpusTags *_tags, const char *_tag, const char *_value)
functions.description: Adds a (tag, value) pair to an initialized OpusTags. Values with embedded NULs are not supported by this helper.
requirements: _tags must be initialized with opus_tags_init() or populated by parse.
_tag must be a NUL-terminated ASCII, case-insensitive tag name without '='.
_value must be a NUL-terminated UTF-8 string (no embedded NULs supported by this API).
On allocation failure returns OP_EFAULT; check return value.

functions.name: opus_tags_add_comment
functions.description: Adds a raw comment string in "TAG=value" form to an initialized OpusTags. Embedded NULs are not supported by this helper.
requirements: _tags must be initialized prior to call.
_comment must be a NUL-terminated UTF-8 string in TAG=value form (no embedded NULs supported by this API).
On allocation failure returns OP_EFAULT; check return value.

functions.name: opus_tags_set_binary_suffix
functions.signature: int opus_tags_set_binary_suffix(OpusTags *_tags, const unsigned char *_data, int _len)
functions.description: Sets or replaces the binary suffix data after the encoded user comments in an OpusTags packet. Pass _len = 0 to remove any existing binary suffix.
requirements: _tags must be initialized.
If _len < 0, returns OP_EINVAL.
If _len > 0: _data must be non-NULL and the least significant bit of _data[0] must be set; otherwise returns OP_EINVAL.
May return OP_EFAULT on allocation failure; check return value.

functions.name: opus_tags_query
functions.signature: const char *opus_tags_query(const OpusTags *_tags, const char *_tag, int _count)
functions.description: Looks up the value for the _count-th occurrence of tag name _tag in an OpusTags. Returns a direct pointer into the OpusTags storage; do not modify or free it.
requirements: _tags must be initialized and populated.
_tag must be a NUL-terminated ASCII tag name (case-insensitive).
_count selects the occurrence index (0-based). Use opus_tags_query_count() to get the valid range.
Returned pointer becomes invalid if the OpusTags is modified or cleared.
Returns NULL if no matching tag or index is out of range.

functions.name: opus_tags_query_count
functions.description: Returns the number of instances of a given tag name in an OpusTags.
requirements: _tags must be initialized and populated.
_tag must be a NUL-terminated ASCII tag name (case-insensitive).

functions.name: opus_tags_get_binary_suffix
functions.description: Retrieves the binary suffix data and length from an OpusTags, if any. Returns NULL if none present.
requirements: _tags must be initialized.
_len must be a valid pointer to receive length.
Returned pointer is owned by OpusTags; do not free or modify and it may be invalidated by later modifications or clear.

functions.name: opus_tags_get_album_gain
functions.description: Parses the first R128_ALBUM_GAIN tag and returns its value in Q8 dB (1/256 dB units) if present and valid. Intended for apps that need to display or apply album gain.
requirements: _tags must be initialized and populated.
_gain_q8 must be a valid pointer to receive the gain value.
On success, value is in [-32768, 32767].
Returns OP_FALSE if no album gain is available; check return value.

functions.name: opus_tags_get_track_gain
functions.description: Parses the first R128_TRACK_GAIN tag and returns its value in Q8 dB (1/256 dB units) if present and valid. Intended for apps that need to display or apply track gain.
requirements: _tags must be initialized and populated.
_gain_q8 must be a valid pointer to receive the gain value.
On success, value is in [-32768, 32767].
Returns OP_FALSE if no track gain is available; check return value.

functions.name: opus_tags_clear
functions.description: Frees all memory used by an OpusTags structure. Call when the tags are no longer needed.
requirements: _tags must be a valid pointer to an OpusTags that was initialized and/or populated.
Do not use pointers previously returned by opus_tags_query()/get_binary_suffix() after clearing.

functions.name: opus_tagcompare
functions.description: Compares a comment string against a tag name (case-insensitive ASCII) to determine if it is an instance of that tag ("tag=value"). Returns <0, 0, or >0 like strcmp-style comparison relative to a matching "tag=value" string.
requirements: _tag_name must be a NUL-terminated ASCII tag name without '='.
_comment must be a NUL-terminated comment string to check.

functions.name: opus_tagncompare
functions.signature: int opus_tagncompare(const char *_tag_name, int _tag_len, const char *_comment)
functions.description: Like opus_tagcompare() but takes a known tag name length for efficiency. Compares the first _tag_len characters of _tag_name against the tag part of "tag=value".
requirements: _tag_len must be non-negative.
_tag_name must reference at least _tag_len characters of a case-insensitive ASCII tag name (no '=').
_comment must be a NUL-terminated comment string to check.

functions.name: opus_picture_tag_parse
functions.description: Parses a METADATA_BLOCK_PICTURE tag (optionally prefixed by "METADATA_BLOCK_PICTURE=") from base64 to an OpusPictureTag, filling MIME type, description, dimensions (if determinable), and raw image data. Attempts to detect JPEG/PNG/GIF and set format; may override parameters from tag if extracted from image data.
requirements: _pic must be an allocated OpusPictureTag; contents left unmodified on failure.
_tag must be a NUL-terminated UTF-8 string with the METADATA_BLOCK_PICTURE content; the leading key is optional.
On success, caller must later free with opus_picture_tag_clear().
Returns OP_ENOTFORMAT if contents invalid; OP_EFAULT on allocation failure.

functions.name: opus_picture_tag_init
functions.description: Initializes an OpusPictureTag so it can be safely populated or cleared later.
requirements: _pic must be a valid pointer to an allocated OpusPictureTag.
Call before parse/fill; clear later with opus_picture_tag_clear().

functions.name: opus_picture_tag_clear
functions.description: Frees all memory referenced by an OpusPictureTag. Call when no longer needed.
requirements: _pic must be a valid pointer to an OpusPictureTag previously initialized.
Do not use internal pointers after clearing.

functions.name: opus_server_info_init
functions.description: Initializes an OpusServerInfo with default values indicating fields not present. Requires linking against libopusurl.
requirements: _info must be a valid pointer to an allocated OpusServerInfo.
Link with libopusurl when using this API.

functions.name: opus_server_info_clear
functions.description: Frees all memory used by an OpusServerInfo. Requires linking against libopusurl.
requirements: _info must be a valid pointer to an OpusServerInfo previously initialized or filled via OP_GET_SERVER_INFO.
Link with libopusurl when using this API.

functions.name: op_fopen
functions.description: Opens a stdio FILE* via fopen() and returns an opaque stream handle plus fills OpusFileCallbacks to access it using 64-bit safe seek/tell. Useful to avoid cross-module FILE* issues and to get portable callbacks.
requirements: _cb must be non-NULL; on error, it is left untouched.
_path must be a valid path (UTF-8 on Windows; native encoding elsewhere).
_mode must be a valid fopen() mode string.
Returns NULL on error; check before using callbacks.

functions.name: op_fdopen
functions.description: Wraps fdopen() to create a stream and fill OpusFileCallbacks for it. Provides portable 64-bit seek/tell callback wrappers.
requirements: _cb must be non-NULL; left untouched on error.
_fd must be a valid file descriptor suitable for fdopen().
_mode must be a valid mode string for fdopen().
Returns NULL on error.

functions.name: op_freopen
functions.signature: void *op_freopen(OpusFileCallbacks *_cb, const char *_path, const char *_mode, void *_stream)
functions.description: Wraps freopen() on an existing stream created by op_fopen/op_fdopen/op_freopen and fills OpusFileCallbacks, returning a new stream handle for use with those callbacks.
requirements: _cb, _path, _mode, and _stream must be non-NULL.
_stream must be a stream previously returned by op_fopen/op_fdopen/op_freopen.
Returns NULL on error; on error _cb is left untouched.

functions.name: op_mem_stream_create
functions.description: Creates a non-seek or seek-capable stream (as implemented internally) that reads from the provided memory block containing the complete stream. Fills callbacks to access it and returns an opaque stream handle.
requirements: _cb must be non-NULL; on error, left untouched.
_data may be NULL only if _size==0 to create an empty stream; typical use passes the full data buffer.
_size is the total number of bytes of the complete stream image.
Returns NULL on error.

functions.name: op_url_stream_vcreate
functions.description: Creates a stream that reads from a URL (file/http/https), filling callbacks for access; takes a va_list of URL options (terminated by NULL). Does not call va_end. Requires linking against libopusurl.
requirements: _cb and _url must be non-NULL.
URL must currently use file:, http:, or https: scheme; http/https may be disabled at compile time.
_ap must be a valid va_list of url_options terminated by NULL; its value is undefined after the call.
Returns NULL on error; on error _cb is left untouched.
Link with libopusurl.

functions.name: op_url_stream_create
functions.description: Creates a stream that reads from a URL (file/http/https), filling callbacks for access; takes variable URL options (terminated by NULL). Requires linking against libopusurl.
requirements: _cb and _url must be non-NULL.
Only file:, http:, and https: supported (http/https may be disabled at build time).
Variadic url_options must be terminated with NULL.
Returns NULL on error; on error _cb is left untouched.
Link with libopusurl.

functions.name: op_test
functions.signature: int op_test(OpusHead *_head, const unsigned char *_initial_data, size_t _initial_bytes)
functions.description: Quickly tests whether the provided initial bytes look like an Opus stream; optionally returns parsed ID header in _head. Intended as a fast rejection filter; does not guarantee full validity.
requirements: Provide at least ~57 bytes for pure Opus-only streams for good results; ~512 bytes recommended for multiplexed streams.
_initial_data must contain data from the start of the stream; length is _initial_bytes.
_head may be NULL if header info not needed; on failure, _head is unmodified.
Check return: 0 means looks like Opus; negative error otherwise (OP_FALSE if insufficient data).

functions.name: op_open_file
functions.description: Opens an Ogg Opus stream from a filesystem path and returns an OggOpusFile handle on success. On error returns NULL and optionally stores an error code in _error.
requirements: _path must be non-NULL and refer to a readable file.
If _error is non-NULL, it receives 0 on success or an error code. If the file could not be opened, _error is OP_EFAULT; otherwise errors are from op_open_callbacks().
Caller must later call op_free() on a successful open.

functions.name: op_open_memory
functions.description: Opens an Ogg Opus stream from a memory buffer and returns an OggOpusFile. On error returns NULL and optionally stores an error code.
requirements: _data must point to a buffer containing the complete stream image; _size is its length.
_error, if non-NULL, receives 0 on success or an error code per op_open_callbacks().
On success, free with op_free().

functions.name: op_vopen_url
functions.description: Opens an Ogg Opus stream from a URL using a va_list of URL options (terminated by NULL). Does not call va_end. Requires linking against libopusurl.
requirements: _url must be non-NULL and use file:, http:, or https: (http/https may be disabled).
_ap must be a valid va_list of url_options terminated by NULL; its value is undefined after the call.
_error, if non-NULL, receives 0 on success or an error code per op_open_callbacks().
On success, free with op_free().
Link with libopusurl.

functions.name: op_open_url
functions.description: Opens an Ogg Opus stream from a URL with variadic URL options (terminated by NULL). Requires linking against libopusurl.
requirements: _url must be non-NULL and use file:, http:, or https: (http/https may be disabled).
Variadic url_options must be terminated with NULL.
_error, if non-NULL, receives 0 on success or an error code per op_open_callbacks().
On success, free with op_free().
Link with libopusurl.

functions.name: op_open_callbacks
functions.signature: OggOpusFile *op_open_callbacks(void *_stream, const OpusFileCallbacks *_cb, const unsigned char *_initial_data, size_t _initial_bytes, int *_error)
functions.description: Opens an Ogg Opus stream using application-provided callbacks for I/O. Supports unseekable and seekable sources. If callbacks include a successful seek(), then tell() must be provided and work consistently. On failure, the stream is not taken over (caller must close it).
requirements: _cb must be non-NULL and its read() must be implemented; seek()/tell() may be NULL or may return -1 to indicate unseekable. If seek() succeeds on this stream, tell() must also be implemented and succeed.
If close() is non-NULL it will be called when op_free() destroys the OggOpusFile; it is not called if op_open_callbacks() itself fails.

_initial_data/_initial_bytes may provide pre-read bytes from the start of the stream. If the stream is seekable, the current position (tell() at entry) must equal _initial_bytes; otherwise absolute seeks will be inconsistent.
_error, if non-NULL, receives an error code on failure (see documented list: OP_EREAD, OP_EFAULT, OP_EIMPL, OP_EINVAL, OP_ENOTFORMAT, OP_EBADHEADER, OP_EVERSION, OP_EBADLINK, OP_EBADTIMESTAMP).
On success, later free with op_free().

functions.name: op_test_file
functions.description: Partially opens a stream from a file path. Loads headers for the first link and tests for seekability but does not fully open or allow decoding. Finish with op_test_open() or free with op_free().
requirements: _path must be non-NULL.
_error, if non-NULL, receives 0 on success or an error code (OP_EFAULT if the file could not be opened; otherwise from op_open_callbacks()).
Only limited queries are available until op_test_open() succeeds.

functions.name: op_test_memory
functions.description: Partially opens a stream from a memory buffer. Loads headers for the first link and tests for seekability but does not fully open or allow decoding. Finish with op_test_open() or free with op_free().
requirements: _data must point to a buffer with the stream image; _size is its length.
_error, if non-NULL, receives 0 on success or an error per op_open_callbacks().

functions.name: op_vtest_url
functions.description: Partially opens a stream from a URL using a va_list of URL options (terminated by NULL). Loads first-link headers and tests for seekability. Requires linking against libopusurl. Finish with op_test_open() or free with op_free().
requirements: _url must be non-NULL and use file:, http:, or https: (http/https may be disabled).
_ap must be a valid va_list of url_options terminated by NULL; value is undefined after the call.
_error, if non-NULL, receives 0 on success or an error per op_open_callbacks().
Link with libopusurl.

functions.name: op_test_url
functions.description: Partially opens a stream from a URL with variadic URL options (terminated by NULL). Loads first-link headers and tests for seekability. Requires linking against libopusurl. Finish with op_test_open() or free with op_free().
requirements: _url must be non-NULL and use file:, http:, or https: (http/https may be disabled).
Variadic url_options must be terminated with NULL.
_error, if non-NULL, receives 0 on success or an error per op_open_callbacks().
Link with libopusurl.

functions.name: op_test_callbacks
functions.signature: OggOpusFile *op_test_callbacks(void *_stream, const OpusFileCallbacks *_cb, const unsigned char *_initial_data, size_t _initial_bytes, int *_error)
functions.description: Partially opens a stream using application-provided callbacks. Tests for Opusness, loads headers for the first link, and tests seekability without fully opening. Only limited queries are available until op_test_open().
requirements: _cb must be non-NULL; read() must be implemented. If seek() succeeds on the source, tell() must also be implemented and succeed.
_initial_data/_initial_bytes can include bytes from the start. If the stream is seekable, the current position at entry must equal _initial_bytes.
_error, if non-NULL, receives 0 on success or an error per op_open_callbacks().
On failure, stream ownership is not taken; caller must close it.

functions.name: op_test_open
functions.description: Finishes opening a stream previously partially opened with op_test_callbacks() or its convenience wrappers. After success the stream supports full operations (decoding, seeking if available).
requirements: _of must be a partially opened OggOpusFile obtained from op_test_* functions.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise a negative error (OP_EREAD, OP_EFAULT, OP_EIMPL, OP_EINVAL, OP_ENOTFORMAT, OP_EBADHEADER, OP_EVERSION, OP_EBADLINK, OP_EBADTIMESTAMP).
Regardless of success, caller must free _of with op_free() eventually.

functions.name: op_free
functions.description: Releases all resources associated with an OggOpusFile. Calls the close() callback if provided during open. Safe to call on partially or fully opened handles.
requirements: _of must be a pointer returned by an op_open_* or op_test_* function (may be NULL for no-op depending on implementation; specification does not state; pass valid pointer).
After calling, the handle must not be used.

functions.name: op_seekable
functions.description: Reports whether the stream is seekable (callbacks support seek/tell and succeeded at least once). May be called on partially-opened streams.
requirements: _of must be non-NULL.
Returns non-zero if seekable, 0 if not.

functions.name: op_link_count
functions.description: Returns the number of links in the chained stream. On partially-opened streams always returns 1; actual count requires fully opened, seekable streams.
requirements: _of must be non-NULL.
For partially-open or unseekable streams, expect return 1.

functions.name: op_serialno
functions.description: Returns the Ogg serial number of the specified link. Negative _li requests the current link. For non-seekable streams always returns the current link's serial number. If _li exceeds the number of links, returns the last link's serial.
requirements: _of must be non-NULL.
_li < 0 selects current link; otherwise selects link by index (out-of-range yields last link).

functions.name: op_channel_count
functions.description: Returns the channel count for the specified link. Negative _li requests the current link. For non-seekable streams always returns the current link's channel count.
requirements: _of must be non-NULL.
_li < 0 selects current link; otherwise selects link by index (out-of-range yields last link).

functions.name: op_raw_total
functions.description: Returns the total compressed byte size of the stream or a specific link (including headers and muxing overhead). For multiplexed streams, this is the entire link size, not just Opus bytes.
requirements: _of must be non-NULL.
Stream must be seekable and fully opened; otherwise returns OP_EINVAL.
_li < 0 requests entire stream; non-negative requests link index; if _li >= link count returns OP_EINVAL.
May be smaller than underlying file size if trailing garbage was detected.

functions.name: op_pcm_total
functions.description: Returns the total number of 48 kHz PCM samples in the stream or a specific link.
requirements: _of must be non-NULL.
Stream must be seekable and fully opened; otherwise returns OP_EINVAL.
_li < 0 requests entire stream; non-negative requests link index; if _li >= link count returns OP_EINVAL.

functions.name: op_head
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the Opus ID header (OpusHead) for the specified link. On partially-opened streams, always returns the first link's header.
requirements: _of must be non-NULL.
_li < 0 selects current link; for unseekable streams, _li is ignored and current link info is returned if available.
Returned pointer is owned by the library; do not free or modify and it may be invalidated after op_free() or after operations affecting metadata caches.

functions.name: op_tags
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the OpusTags for the specified link, or NULL for unseekable streams that encountered an invalid link. On partially-opened streams, always returns the first link's tags.
requirements: _of must be non-NULL.
_li < 0 selects current link; for unseekable streams, _li is ignored and current link info is returned if available.
Returned pointer is owned by the library; do not free or modify. May be NULL if invalid.

functions.name: op_current_link
functions.description: Returns the index of the current link (the one most recently decoded from, or reached by a seek). For unseekable streams, starts at 0 and increments at each new link. Returns OP_EINVAL if the stream is only partially open.
requirements: _of must be non-NULL.
Do not call on a partially opened stream if you expect a non-negative index; check for OP_EINVAL.

functions.name: op_bitrate
functions.description: Computes the average bitrate (bits per second) of the entire stream or a specific link. Requires a seekable, fully opened stream.
requirements: _of must be non-NULL and fully opened.
Stream must be seekable; otherwise returns OP_EINVAL.
_li < 0 for whole stream, non-negative for link index; if _li >= link count returns OP_EINVAL.
For multiplexed streams, uses the total stream/link size (not Opus-only).

functions.name: op_bitrate_instant
functions.description: Returns the instantaneous bitrate since the last call/seek/start. May spike after seeks or chain boundaries due to pre-skip/pre-roll/end-trim. Returns OP_FALSE if no data has been decoded yet; OP_EINVAL if only partially open.
requirements: _of must be non-NULL and at least fully opened for decoding.
Interpreting negative return values as errors is required (OP_FALSE, OP_EINVAL).

functions.name: op_raw_tell
functions.description: Returns the current byte position being read from. Returns OP_EINVAL if the stream is only partially open.
requirements: _of must be non-NULL.
Do not call on a partially opened stream if you expect a position; check for OP_EINVAL.

functions.name: op_pcm_tell
functions.description: Returns the current 48 kHz PCM offset of the next sample to be read. On ill-timestamped streams, this may not be strictly monotonic. Returns OP_EINVAL if only partially open.
requirements: _of must be non-NULL.
Do not call on a partially opened stream if you expect a valid offset; check for OP_EINVAL.

functions.name: op_raw_seek
functions.description: Seeks to a byte position within the compressed data, scanning packets to update the PCM cursor. Fast (at most one physical seek). May cross a logical bitstream boundary if necessary.
requirements: _of must be non-NULL and refer to a seekable, fully opened stream.
_byte_offset must be within [0, op_raw_total(_of, -1)].
Returns 0 on success or a negative error: OP_EREAD, OP_EINVAL (partially open or out of range), OP_ENOSEEK (unseekable), OP_EBADLINK.

functions.name: op_pcm_seek
functions.description: Seeks to an exact 48 kHz PCM sample offset so that subsequent decoding begins at the requested position. Handles required decoder pre-roll internally.
requirements: _of must be non-NULL and refer to a seekable, fully opened stream.
_pcm_offset must be within the valid PCM range of the stream.
Returns 0 on success or a negative error: OP_EREAD, OP_EINVAL (partially open or out of range), OP_ENOSEEK (unseekable), OP_EBADLINK.

functions.name: op_set_decode_callback
functions.description: Registers a per-packet decode callback. If set, libopusfile invokes it for each packet needing decoding, allowing advanced processing or custom decoding. The callback may return OP_DEC_USE_DEFAULT to let libopusfile decode normally.
requirements: _of must be non-NULL.
_decode_cb may be NULL to disable the callback.
Callback must fill exactly nsamples*nchannels in the requested format when returning success (0).
Callback errors should mirror opus_multistream_decode[_float] error codes.

functions.name: op_set_gain_offset
functions.description: Controls the playback gain. Selects how to combine header gain and optional R128 album/track gain with an additional offset (Q8 dB). Total gain is clamped to [-32768,32767]/256 dB. New gain does not retroactively affect buffered decoded audio.
requirements: _of must be non-NULL.
_gain_type must be one of OP_HEADER_GAIN, OP_ALBUM_GAIN, OP_TRACK_GAIN, or OP_ABSOLUTE_GAIN; otherwise returns OP_EINVAL.
_gain_offset_q8 is in 1/256 dB units.
Do not expect sample-by-sample gain changes; at best updates per packet.

functions.name: op_set_dither_enabled
functions.description: Enables or disables noise-shaping dithering when producing 16-bit samples via op_read()/op_read_stereo() in floating-point builds. Has no effect when using op_read_float()/op_read_float_stereo() or when built for fixed-point decoding.
requirements: _of must be non-NULL.
_enabled: non-zero enables dithering; 0 disables.

functions.name: op_read
functions.description: Decodes and returns interleaved 16-bit PCM samples at 48 kHz. Returns the number of samples per channel. Channel count may change at chain boundaries; optionally returns the link index in *_li.
requirements: _of must be non-NULL and fully opened (not just partially).
_pcm must have room for at least _buf_size 16-bit values; returned count is per channel, not total values.
_buf_size should ideally allow ≥120 ms per channel (5760 values/channel) to reduce buffering; smaller is allowed but may return fewer samples.
_li may be NULL if link index is not needed; on error it is left unset.
Check negative returns for errors (listed in header), including OP_EREAD (e.g., https truncation), OP_EINVAL (partially open), OP_EBADPACKET, etc.

functions.name: op_read_float
functions.description: Decodes and returns interleaved 32-bit float PCM samples at 48 kHz, with nominal range [-1.0, 1.0]. Returns the number of samples per channel. Channel count may change at chain boundaries; optionally returns the link index.
requirements: _of must be non-NULL and fully opened (not just partially).
_pcm must have room for at least _buf_size floats; returned count is per channel.

import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

def _le16(u: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<H', u & 0xFFFF)

def _le32(u: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<I', u & 0xFFFFFFFF)

def _clamp(v: int, lo: int, hi: int) -> int:
    return lo if v < lo else hi if v > hi else v

# Build an Opus ID header (per RFC 7845 / libopusfile expectations)
# Layout (little-endian):
#  0..7   magic: "OpusHead"
#  8      version (0..255)
#  9      channel_count (1..255, but libopusfile typical 1..8)
# 10..11  pre_skip (LE16)
# 12..15  input_sample_rate (LE32, informational; often 0 or original)
# 16..17  output_gain (LE16 signed Q8 dB)
# 18      mapping_family (0,1, or 255 reserved/rejected)
# 19      stream_count (if mapping_family != 0)
# 20      coupled_count (if mapping_family != 0)
# 21..    mapping[channels] (if mapping_family != 0)
# For mapping_family==0, there are no stream/coupled/mapping bytes.
# libopusfile rejects mapping_family 255 in general-purpose mode; to exercise success paths use 0 or 1.

# Provide a few interesting valid variants:
# - Mono, stereo, surround up to 8 channels
# - mapping family 0 (implicit) and 1 (explicit Vorbis order mapping)
# - Various pre-skip, sample rate (0 and common rates), and output gain values

# Channel mapping presets for mapping_family=1: mapping tables from RFC (Vorbis order)
# For simplicity we include valid tables for up to 8 channels.
_MAPPING_FAM1: dict[int, Tuple[int, int, List[int]]] = {
    # channels: (stream_count, coupled_count, mapping[channels])
    1: (1, 0, [0]),
    2: (1, 1, [0, 1]),
    3: (2, 1, [0, 2, 1]),                  # L, C, R
    4: (2, 2, [0, 1, 2, 3]),               # FL, FR, RL, RR
    5: (3, 2, [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]),            # FL, FR, FC, RL, RR
    6: (4, 2, [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]),         # FL, FR, FC, LFE, RL, RR
    7: (4, 3, [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]),
    8: (5, 3, [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]),
}

_COMMON_SAMPLE_RATES = [0, 8000, 12000, 16000, 24000, 44100, 48000, 96000]

def _build_header(version: int,
                  channels: int,
                  pre_skip: int,
                  input_rate: int,
                  gain_q8: int,
                  mapping_family: int,
                  rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    b = bytearray()
    b += b"OpusHead"
    b.append(version & 0xFF)
    b.append(channels & 0xFF)
    b += _le16(pre_skip)
    b += _le32(input_rate)
    # gain is signed 16-bit Q8 dB; clamp to int16 range
    gain_q8 = _clamp(gain_q8, -32768, 32767)
    b += struct.pack('<h', gain_q8)
    b.append(mapping_family & 0xFF)

    if mapping_family == 0:
        # No stream_count/coupled_count/mapping[]
        return bytes(b)

    # mapping_family == 1: include counts and mapping table
    # Ensure we have a valid preset; if not, fall back to stereo
    if channels not in _MAPPING_FAM1:
        channels = 2
    stream_count, coupled_count, mapping = _MAPPING_FAM1[channels]
    b.append(stream_count & 0xFF)
    b.append(coupled_count & 0xFF)
    # Optionally shuffle mapping occasionally while keeping it a permutation of 0..channels-1
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        mapping = mapping[:]  # copy
        rng.shuffle(mapping)
    b += bytes(int(x) & 0xFF for x in mapping[:channels])
    return bytes(b)

def _pick_channels(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Bias towards common cases but include up to 8
    choices = [1, 2, 2, 2, 5, 6, 8, 3, 4, 7]
    return choices[rng.randrange(len(choices))]

def _pick_version(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # 1 is common today; 0 also valid historically; include some random bytes
    return rng.choices([0, 1, rng.randrange(0, 256)], weights=[2, 5, 1], k=1)[0]

def _pick_preskip(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Typical Opus pre-skip ~ 312..3840 samples; include 0 and larger values
    options = [0, 80, 312, 384, 960, 2560, 3840, 8000]
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        return rng.randrange(0, 10000)
    return rng.choice(options)

def _pick_rate(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        return rng.choice(_COMMON_SAMPLE_RATES)
    return rng.randrange(0, 200000)

def _pick_gain_q8(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Include 0, small positives/negatives, extremes
    choices = [0, 0, 0, 256, -256, 20*256, -20*256, 32767, -32768]
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        return rng.randrange(-40000, 40000)
    return rng.choice(choices)

def _pick_mapping_family(channels: int, rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Favor valid families 0 and 1; occasionally choose 1 for multichannel
    if channels <= 2:
        return 0 if rng.random() < 0.7 else 1
    return 1 if rng.random() < 0.9 else 0

def _maybe_pad(rng: random.Random, header: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Some callers pass larger pkt sizes; allow optional padding/trailing bytes that lib ignores
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        pad_len = rng.randrange(0, 16)
        return header + rng.randbytes(pad_len)
    return header

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose parameters
    channels = _pick_channels(rng)
    version = _pick_version(rng)
    pre_skip = _pick_preskip(rng)
    input_rate = _pick_rate(rng)
    gain_q8 = _pick_gain_q8(rng)
    mapping_family = _pick_mapping_family(channels, rng)

    header = _build_header(version, channels, pre_skip, input_rate, gain_q8, mapping_family, rng)
    header = _maybe_pad(rng, header)

    # Ensure upper bound for fuzzer constraints
    if len(header) > 4096:
        header = header[:4096]
    return header

# This generator produces a valid OpusTags header packet as used by libopusfile.
# Layout (little-endian):
#  bytes 0..7   : ASCII "OpusTags"
#  4 bytes LE   : vendor_length (uint32)
#  vendor_length bytes: vendor string (UTF-8, no terminating NUL)
#  4 bytes LE   : user_comment_list_length (uint32)
#  For each comment:
#    4 bytes LE : length N (uint32)
#    N bytes    : UTF-8 text "TAG=value" (no terminating NUL)
#  1 byte       : framing bit (0x01)
# OpusTags in Opus requires the framing bit present (Vorbis-style comment framing).

MAX_TOTAL_SIZE = 4096
MAGIC = b"OpusTags"

# We'll embed a tiny, syntactically valid FLAC PICTURE block in base64 so downstream picture parsing can succeed when present.
# FLAC PICTURE block layout (per spec):
# 32-bit BE type, 32-bit BE MIME length, MIME, 32-bit BE desc length, desc,
# 32-bit BE width, height, depth, colors, 32-bit BE data length, data

def be32(n: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">I", n & 0xFFFFFFFF)

def make_flac_picture_block(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed ^ 0xA5A5_5A5A)
    # Choose a type (3 = cover front)
    pic_type = rnd.choice([0, 3])
    mime = rnd.choice([b"image/png", b"image/jpeg", b"-->"])  # "-->" indicates URL according to spec
    desc = rnd.choice([b"Cover", b"Front", b"Artwork", b""])

    if mime == b"image/png":
        data = b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n" + b"minimal"
    elif mime == b"image/jpeg":
        data = b"\xFF\xD8\xFF\xE0" + b"JFIF\x00" + b"mini"
    else:
        # URL case stores a URL as data
        data = b"http://example.com/cover.jpg"
    width = rnd.randrange(16, 1024)
    height = rnd.randrange(16, 1024)
    depth = rnd.choice([8, 24])
    colors = 0
    blob = b"".join([
        be32(pic_type),
        be32(len(mime)), mime,
        be32(len(desc)), desc,
        be32(width), be32(height), be32(depth), be32(colors),
        be32(len(data)), data,
    ])
    return blob

def rand_string(rnd: random.Random, choices: List[str], fallback: str) -> str:
    return rnd.choice(choices) if choices else fallback

def make_text_comment(tag: str, value: str) -> str:
    return f"{tag}={value}"

def make_gain_value_q8(rnd: random.Random) -> str:

    # Opusfile parsers accept integer Q8 via helper getters; textual tag typically like "R128_TRACK_GAIN=-1234" in Q8.

    style = rnd.randrange(3)

        return str(rnd.randrange(-32768, 32768))
    elif style == 1:
        # Decimal dB to two decimals
        val_db = rnd.uniform(-20.0, 20.0)
        return f"{val_db:.2f} dB"
    else:
        # Signed with no unit
        val_db = rnd.uniform(-18.0, 18.0)
        return f"{val_db:.2f}"

def build_opustags_packet(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    # Decide sizes within budget
    target_size = rnd.randrange(64, min(1024, MAX_TOTAL_SIZE))

    vendor = rand_string(rnd, VENDORS, "libopus").encode("utf-8")

    comments: List[bytes] = []

    # Core descriptive tags
    if rnd.random() < 0.9:
        title = rand_string(rnd, TITLES, "Track"); comments.append(make_text_comment("TITLE", title).encode("utf-8"))
    if rnd.random() < 0.9:
        artist = rand_string(rnd, ARTISTS, "Artist"); comments.append(make_text_comment("ARTIST", artist).encode("utf-8"))
    if rnd.random() < 0.7:
        album = rand_string(rnd, ALBUMS, "Album"); comments.append(make_text_comment("ALBUM", album).encode("utf-8"))
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        comments.append(make_text_comment("GENRE", rand_string(rnd, GENRES, "Other")).encode("utf-8"))
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        comments.append(make_text_comment("DATE", str(rnd.randrange(1990, 2026))).encode("utf-8"))
    if rnd.random() < 0.4:
        comments.append(make_text_comment("TRACKNUMBER", str(rnd.randrange(1, 25))).encode("utf-8"))

    # Gains
    if rnd.random() < 0.6:
        comments.append(make_text_comment("R128_TRACK_GAIN", make_gain_value_q8(rnd)).encode("utf-8"))
    if rnd.random() < 0.6:
        comments.append(make_text_comment("R128_ALBUM_GAIN", make_gain_value_q8(rnd)).encode("utf-8"))

    # A free-form comment
    if rnd.random() < 0.6:
        comments.append(make_text_comment("COMMENT", rand_string(rnd, DESCRIPTIONS, "Sample")).encode("utf-8"))

    # Optionally include a METADATA_BLOCK_PICTURE with a valid base64 FLAC picture block
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        pic_block = make_flac_picture_block(seed)
        pic_b64 = base64.b64encode(pic_block).decode("ascii")
        comments.append(make_text_comment("METADATA_BLOCK_PICTURE", pic_b64).encode("utf-8"))

    # Assemble packet while respecting MAX_TOTAL_SIZE
    parts: List[bytes] = [MAGIC]
    parts.append(struct.pack("<I", len(vendor)))
    parts.append(vendor)
    # We'll add comments incrementally and ensure size with framing bit fits.

    comment_entries: List[Tuple[int, bytes]] = []

        # Rebuild minimally with zero comments
        parts = [MAGIC, struct.pack("<I", len(vendor)), vendor, struct.pack("<I", 0), b"\x01"]

# - Tags: produce a variety of common and edge-case Vorbis/Opus tag names (ASCII, case-insensitive),

    "Recorded live",

]

def _rand_tag(rng: random.Random) -> str:

def _rand_value(rng: random.Random, tag: str) -> str:
    # Prefer values that match tag semantics
    upper = tag.upper()
    if upper in ("R128_TRACK_GAIN", "R128_ALBUM_GAIN"):
        return rng.choice(DB_VALUES)
    if upper in ("TRACKNUMBER", "DISCNUMBER"):
        return rng.choice(["1", "2", "3", "07", "10"])  # simple numerics
    if upper in ("DATE",):
        # ISO-like dates
        year = rng.randint(1970, 2025)
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            return f"{year}"
        month = rng.randint(1, 12)
        day = rng.randint(1, 28)
        return f"{year:04d}-{month:02d}-{day:02d}"
    if upper in ("GENRE",):
        return rng.choice(["Rock", "Electronic", "Classical", "Jazz", "Podcast"]) 
    if upper in ("METADATA_BLOCK_PICTURE",):
        # For opus_tags_add, arbitrary UTF-8 is fine (not base64 here). Provide a plausible description.

        # ReplayGain conventional decimal with dB suffix
        return rng.choice(["-7.50 dB", "0 dB", "+1.25 dB", "-18.00 dB"]) 
    if upper in ("TITLE", "ARTIST", "ALBUM", "ALBUMARTIST", "COMPOSER", "PERFORMER"):
        return rng.choice(UTF8_SAMPLES)
    if upper in ("URL",):
        return rng.choice(URLS)
    # Fallback: random valid UTF-8 string from pool or constructed
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        return rng.choice(TEXT_VALUES)
    # Construct a mixed ASCII/Unicode string
    base = rng.choice(UTF8_SAMPLES)
    extra = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + ' -._/') for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 16)))
    return (base + (" " + extra if extra else "")).strip()


def _make_cstrings(tag: str, value: str) -> bytes:
    # Ensure both are UTF-8 encodable and contain no NULs
    tag = tag.replace('\x00', '')
    value = value.replace('\x00', '')
    tb = tag.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00"
    vb = value.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00"
    return tb + vb


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Sometimes bias toward gain-related tags to exercise gain parsing in later queries
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        tag = rng.choice(["R128_TRACK_GAIN", "R128_ALBUM_GAIN"]) 
    else:
        tag = _rand_tag(rng)

    value = _rand_value(rng, tag)

    buf = _make_cstrings(tag, value)

    # If buffer is too small to be interesting, extend value with additional info but keep valid UTF-8
    if len(buf) < 8:
        extra = rng.choice(TEXT_VALUES)
        buf = _make_cstrings(tag, value + " " + extra)

    # Enforce max size
    if len(buf) > 4096:
        # Truncate value portion carefully before the terminating NUL
        # Find first NUL (end of tag), keep tag, trim value to fit
        first_nul = buf.find(b"\x00")
        if first_nul == -1:
            # Should not happen, but ensure at least proper termination
            buf = buf[:4095] + b"\x00"
        else:
            tag_part = buf[: first_nul + 1]
            space_left = 4096 - len(tag_part) - 1  # leave 1 for final NUL
            if space_left < 0:
                # Fallback: keep just tag and empty value
                buf = tag_part + b"\x00"
            else:
                value_bytes = value.encode('utf-8')
                value_bytes = value_bytes[:space_left]
                buf = tag_part + value_bytes + b"\x00"

    return buf

# Generator for valid OpusTags binary suffix blobs
# Target stub uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR() for the data pointer and integers for length.
# Constraints:
# - When len > 0, first byte must have LSB set (bit 0 = 1).
# - len can be 0 (remove), positive (set), or negative (error). We provide bytes that
#   are useful when positive, while the harness chooses len itself.
# - Provide interesting, but valid, binary payloads that exercise different paths.
#
# We return a bytes buffer that the harness will use for FUZZ_PARAM_STR().
# Keep size <= 4096.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

KNOWN_MAGIC_PREFIXES = [
    b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n",            # PNG signature
    b"\xff\xd8\xff\xe0JFIF\x00",      # JPEG JFIF
    b"\xff\xd8\xff\xe1Exif\x00\x00", # JPEG EXIF
    b"GIF87a",                            # GIF87a
    b"GIF89a",                            # GIF89a
]

# Construct a variety of valid-looking binary blobs with first byte LSB=1.
# While the binary suffix is opaque to the parser besides the first-byte LSB rule,
# different sizes and contents may exercise allocation/copy paths.

def _ensure_lsb1(b: bytearray) -> bytearray:
    if not b:
        b.extend(b"\x01")
    else:
        b[0] |= 0x01
    return b

def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytearray:
    return bytearray(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _make_png_like(rng: random.Random, size: int) -> bytearray:
    # Create a minimal PNG-like structure with proper signature then pad.
    data = bytearray(KNOWN_MAGIC_PREFIXES[0])
    # IHDR chunk (length 13 + type + CRC placeholder). We'll not compute CRC; suffix treats as opaque.
    ihdr = bytearray()
    ihdr.extend(struct.pack(">I", 13))
    ihdr.extend(b"IHDR")
    ihdr.extend(struct.pack(">I", rng.randrange(16, 4096)))  # width
    ihdr.extend(struct.pack(">I", rng.randrange(16, 4096)))  # height
    ihdr.extend(bytes([8]))  # bit depth
    ihdr.extend(bytes([6]))  # color type (RGBA)
    ihdr.extend(bytes([0, 0, 0]))  # compression, filter, interlace
    ihdr.extend(struct.pack(">I", 0))  # fake CRC
    data.extend(ihdr)
    # Pad to requested size
    if len(data) < size:
        data.extend(_rand_bytes(rng, size - len(data)))
    return data[:size]

def _make_jpeg_like(rng: random.Random, size: int) -> bytearray:
    data = bytearray(b"\xff\xd8\xff\xe0JFIF\x00\x01\x02\x00\x00\x01\x00\x01\x00\x00")
    # Add some entropy and a fake SOS marker
    data.extend(_rand_bytes(rng, max(0, size - len(data) - 4)))
    data.extend(b"\xff\xda\x00\x08")
    return data[:size]

def _make_gif_like(rng: random.Random, size: int) -> bytearray:
    hdr = rng.choice([b"GIF87a", b"GIF89a"]) + struct.pack("<HH", rng.randrange(1, 512), rng.randrange(1, 512)) + b"\x80\x00\x00"
    data = bytearray(hdr)
    if len(data) < size:
        data.extend(_rand_bytes(rng, size - len(data)))
    return data[:size]

def _make_random_blob(rng: random.Random, size: int) -> bytearray:
    return _rand_bytes(rng, size)

def _make_repeating_pattern(rng: random.Random, size: int) -> bytearray:
    patterns = [
        b"\x01", b"\xff", b"\x55", b"\xaa", b"OpusSuffix", b"\x00\x01\x02\x03\x04\x05\x06\x07",
    ]
    p = rng.choice(patterns)
    reps = (size + len(p) - 1) // len(p)
    return bytearray((p * reps)[:size])

def _make_structured_blob(rng: random.Random, size: int) -> bytearray:
    # Length-prefixed fields and some base64 data to simulate rich content
    fields = []
    def add_field(tag: bytes, payload: bytes):
        fields.append(struct.pack("<H", len(tag)) + tag)
        fields.append(struct.pack("<I", len(payload)))
        fields.append(payload)
    add_field(b"type", rng.choice([b"opaque", b"image/png", b"image/jpeg", b"application/x-custom"]))
    add_field(b"flags", struct.pack("<I", rng.getrandbits(16)))
    rnd_payload = _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randrange(8, 128))
    add_field(b"b64", base64.b64encode(rnd_payload))
    blob = bytearray().join(fields)
    if len(blob) < size:
        blob.extend(_rand_bytes(rng, size - len(blob)))
    return blob[:size]

def _choose_size(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Bias toward small sizes but include a few larger ones to exercise allocation
    choices = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256, 512, 1024, 2048]
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        # Occasionally pick an arbitrary size up to MAX_SIZE
        return rng.randrange(0, min(MAX_SIZE, 3000))
    return rng.choice(choices)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide strategy for content
    strategies = [
        "png", "jpeg", "gif", "random", "repeat", "structured"
    ]
    strat = rng.choice(strategies)

    size = _choose_size(rng)

    if size == 0:
        # Even if harness might select len>0, we still return something minimal; but we'll keep size 0 here
        data = bytearray()
    else:
        if strat == "png":
            data = _make_png_like(rng, size)
        elif strat == "jpeg":
            data = _make_jpeg_like(rng, size)
        elif strat == "gif":
            data = _make_gif_like(rng, size)
        elif strat == "repeat":
            data = _make_repeating_pattern(rng, size)
        elif strat == "structured":
            data = _make_structured_blob(rng, size)
        else:
            data = _make_random_blob(rng, size)

    # Enforce the API rule: first byte LSB must be set when len > 0.
    # We do this unconditionally when size>0; harmless if harness uses len==0.
    data = _ensure_lsb1(bytearray(data))

    # Ensure max size constraint
    if len(data) > MAX_SIZE:
        data = data[:MAX_SIZE]

    return bytes(data)

    # Create a minimal, valid PNG (IHDR + IDAT + IEND). Compute CRCs properly.
    import zlib

    width = rng.randint(min_w, max(1, min_w) + 63)
    height = rng.randint(min_h, max(1, min_h) + 63)
    bit_depth = _rand_choice(rng, [8, 16])
    color_type = _rand_choice(rng, [2, 6])  # Truecolor or Truecolor+alpha
    compression = 0
    filter_method = 0
    interlace = _rand_choice(rng, [0, 1])

    ihdr_data = struct.pack(
        ">IIBBBBB",
        width,
        height,
        bit_depth,
        color_type,
        compression,
        filter_method,
        interlace,
    )

    def chunk(ctype: bytes, cdata: bytes) -> bytes:
        return _be32(len(cdata)) + ctype + cdata + _be32(zlib.crc32(ctype + cdata) & 0xFFFFFFFF)

    # Minimal IDAT with a small zlib stream: one empty scanline with filter 0.
    channels = {0: 1, 2: 3, 3: 1, 4: 2, 6: 4}[color_type]
    bpp = channels * (2 if bit_depth == 16 else 1)
    scanline = bytes([0]) + bytes(width * bpp)
    z = zlib.compress(scanline, 9)

    png = PNG_SIG + chunk(b"IHDR", ihdr_data) + chunk(b"IDAT", z) + chunk(b"IEND", b"")

    depth = bit_depth
    colors = 0
    return png, width, height, depth, colors


def _make_gif(rng: random.Random, min_w: int, min_h: int) -> Tuple[bytes, int, int, int, int]:
    # Generate a minimal single-frame GIF89a/87a with global color table.
    sig = _rand_choice(rng, [GIF87a, GIF89a])
    width = rng.randint(min_w, max(1, min_w) + 63)
    height = rng.randint(min_h, max(1, min_h) + 63)
    gct_flag = 1
    color_res = 7  # 8 bits per channel
    sort_flag = 0
    gct_size_pow = _rand_choice(rng, [0, 1, 2, 3])  # 2,4,8,16 colors
    gct_size_val = (1 << (gct_size_pow + 1))
    packed = (gct_flag << 7) | (color_res << 4) | (sort_flag << 3) | gct_size_pow
    bg_index = 0
    pixel_aspect = 0

    # Global Color Table
    gct = bytearray()
    for _ in range(gct_size_val):
        gct += bytes([rng.randrange(256), rng.randrange(256), rng.randrange(256)])

    lsd = struct.pack("<HHBBB", width, height, packed, bg_index, pixel_aspect)

    # Image Descriptor
    left = top = 0
    lct_flags = 0
    img_desc = b"\x2C" + struct.pack("<HHHHB", left, top, width, height, lct_flags)

    # Minimal LZW image data: LZW min code size and one empty block then terminator
    lzw_min = max(2, gct_size_pow + 1)
    img_data = bytes([lzw_min, 1, 0, 0])  # one sub-block of size 1 (dummy), then terminator 0

    trailer = b"\x3B"

    gif = sig + lsd + gct + img_desc + img_data + trailer

    depth = 8
    colors = gct_size_val
    return gif, width, height, depth, colors


def _make_jpeg(rng: random.Random, min_w: int, min_h: int) -> Tuple[bytes, int, int, int, int]:
    # Construct a tiny baseline JPEG. While not guaranteed universally valid, it's commonly accepted.
    def be16(x):
        return struct.pack(">H", x & 0xFFFF)

    width = rng.randint(min_w, max(1, min_w) + 63)
    height = rng.randint(min_h, max(1, min_h) + 63)

    soi = b"\xFF\xD8"
    app0 = b"\xFF\xE0" + be16(16) + b"JFIF\x00\x01\x02\x00\x00\x01\x00\x01\x00\x00"
    dqt = b"\xFF\xDB" + be16(67) + b"\x00" + bytes([
        16,11,10,16,24,40,51,61,
        12,12,14,19,26,58,60,55,
        14,13,16,24,40,57,69,56,
        14,17,22,29,51,87,80,62,
        18,22,37,56,68,109,103,77,
        24,35,55,64,81,104,113,92,
        49,64,78,87,103,121,120,101,
        72,92,95,98,112,100,103,99
    ])
    sof0 = b"\xFF\xC0" + be16(11) + b"\x08" + be16(height) + be16(width) + b"\x01\x01\x11\x00"
    # Simplified DHT (not a full valid table for all decoders, but acceptable for many)
    dht = b"\xFF\xC4" + be16(0x1F + 0x1F + 2) + b"\x00" + b"\x00"*0x1F + b"\x01\x01" + b"\x10" + b"\x00"*0x1F
    sos = b"\xFF\xDA" + be16(8) + b"\x01\x01\x00\x00\x3F\x00"
    entropy = bytes([0x0F, 0xD2, 0x4A, 0x55, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x00])
    eoi = b"\xFF\xD9"

    jpeg = soi + app0 + dqt + sof0 + dht + sos + entropy + eoi
    depth = 8
    colors = 0
    return jpeg, width, height, depth, colors


def _build_picture_block(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Choose picture type
    pic_type = _rand_choice(rng, [0, 3])  # 0: Other, 3: Front Cover

    # Choose MIME and image generator
    kind = _rand_choice(rng, ["png", "gif", "jpeg", "url"])

    if kind == "png":
        img, w, h, depth, colors = _make_png(rng, 1, 1)
        mime = b"image/png"
    elif kind == "gif":
        img, w, h, depth, colors = _make_gif(rng, 1, 1)
        mime = b"image/gif"
    elif kind == "jpeg":
        img, w, h, depth, colors = _make_jpeg(rng, 1, 1)
        mime = b"image/jpeg"
    else:
        # URL case uses mime '-->' and data is a URL string
        url_schemes = [b"http://", b"https://"]
        host = b"example.com/"
        path = f"cover{rng.randrange(1,1000)}.jpg".encode()
        img = _rand_choice(rng, url_schemes) + host + path
        w = h = 0
        depth = 24
        colors = 0
        mime = b"-->"

    # Optional description
    descriptions = [b"", b"Front cover", b"Album art", b"Cover"]
    desc = _rand_choice(rng, descriptions)

    # Build the METADATA_BLOCK_PICTURE binary
    parts = []
    parts.append(_be32(pic_type))
    parts.append(_be32(len(mime)))
    parts.append(mime)
    parts.append(_be32(len(desc)))
    parts.append(desc)
    parts.append(_be32(w))
    parts.append(_be32(h))
    parts.append(_be32(depth))
    parts.append(_be32(colors))
    parts.append(_be32(len(img)))
    parts.append(img)

    return b"".join(parts)


def _maybe_prefix(rng: random.Random, b64: bytes) -> bytes:
    if rng.getrandbits(1):
        return b"METADATA_BLOCK_PICTURE=" + b64
    return b64


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Generate between 1 and 2 concatenated picture tags separated by newlines.
    count = rng.randint(1, 2)
    payloads = []
    for _ in range(count):
        blob = _build_picture_block(rng)
        b64 = base64.b64encode(blob)
        payloads.append(_maybe_prefix(rng, b64))

    out = b"\n".join(payloads)

    # Ensure size <= 4096
    if len(out) > 4096:
        out = out[:4096]

    return out

# This generator focuses on producing valid filesystem paths suitable for fopen/freopen
# for the target fuzzer stubs using FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME(). The returned bytes will be the
# path string encoded in UTF-8 and NUL-terminated to be robust when passed to C APIs.
#
# Strategy:
# - Create a temporary-like directory structure under a pseudo root inside the current
#   working directory name space (no actual file IO performed here; the fuzzer harness
#   will materialize the provided filename with contents as it sees fit).
# - Generate a variety of interesting path shapes: absolute/relative, with/without
#   directories, extensions commonly used for Opus/Ogg, hidden files, long components,
#   and edge-case characters that are generally valid on POSIX and commonly acceptable
#   on Windows UTF-8 wrappers (excluding reserved characters that fopen() would reject
#   like NUL or path separators within a component where inappropriate).
# - Keep path length well under 4096 bytes.
#
# Note: We avoid any actual filesystem operations as required.

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ ."

EXTS = [
    "opus", "ogg", "oga", "ogx", "spx", "flac", "wav", "txt", "bin"
]

DIR_NAMES = [
    "tmp", "var", "data", "inputs", "samples", "case", "a", "b", "longdir",
    "..hidden", "Music", "音楽", "测试", "スペース 含む"
]

FILE_BASES = [
    "test", "sample", "stream", "opus", "music", "radio", "station",
    "Picture", "cover", "tags", "idheader", "linkchain", "Σ", "диск", "archivo"
]

WINDOWS_FORBIDDEN = set('<>:"|?*')


def _rand_name(rng: random.Random, base_choices: List[str], min_len=1, max_len=16) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.6 and base_choices:
        base = rng.choice(base_choices)
    else:
        length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
        base = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(length)).strip()
        if not base:
            base = "x"
    # Avoid trailing dots/spaces on Windows which can be problematic
    base = base.rstrip(' .') or "x"
    # Avoid reserved names on Windows
    reserved = {"CON","PRN","AUX","NUL","COM1","COM2","COM3","COM4","COM5","COM6","COM7","COM8","COM9",
                "LPT1","LPT2","LPT3","LPT4","LPT5","LPT6","LPT7","LPT8","LPT9"}
    if base.upper() in reserved:
        base = base + "_"
    # Avoid forbidden chars
    base = ''.join(ch for ch in base if ch not in WINDOWS_FORBIDDEN)
    return base or "x"


def _make_components(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    comps = []
    depth = rng.randint(0, 3)
    for _ in range(depth):
        name = _rand_name(rng, DIR_NAMES, 1, rng.randint(4, 18))
        # Occasionally add a dot-prefixed hidden directory
        if rng.random() < 0.2 and not name.startswith('.'):
            name = '.' + name
        comps.append(name)
    return comps


def _make_filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    name = _rand_name(rng, FILE_BASES, 1, rng.randint(4, 24))
    # Optional multi-dot filenames
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        name = name + "." + _rand_name(rng, FILE_BASES, 1, 8)
    # Choose extension with bias towards Opus/Ogg
    if rng.random() < 0.9:
        ext = rng.choices(EXTS, weights=[6,6,2,1,1,1,1,1,1], k=1)[0]
        name = f"{name}.{ext}"
    return name


def _maybe_absolute(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Produce absolute or relative paths according to platform flavors
    style = rng.choice(["posix", "win", "rel"]) if rng.random() < 0.8 else "rel"
    if style == "posix":
        return "/"
    if style == "win":
        drive = rng.choice(list("ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"))
        return f"{drive}:/"  # forward slash acceptable in many runtimes; avoids escaping backslashes
    return ""  # relative


def _join(components: List[str]) -> str:
    # Use forward slashes for portability
    return "/".join(components)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide path root type and components
    root = _maybe_absolute(rng)
    comps = []

    # Occasionally start with current dir or parent references for relative paths
    if root == "":
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            comps.append(".")
        if rng.random() < 0.1:
            comps.append("..")

    # Build directory components
    comps += _make_components(rng)

    # Optionally insert an "interesting" directory name hinting content-type
    if rng.random() < 0.35:
        comps.append(rng.choice(["opus", "ogg", "audio", "streams", "covers"]))

    # Add filename
    filename = _make_filename(rng)
    comps.append(filename)

    path = (root + _join([c for c in comps if c != ""])) if root else _join([c for c in comps if c != ""])

    # Limit length and sanitize to avoid trailing spaces/dots
    if len(path) > 3800:
        path = path[:3800].rstrip(' .')
    if not path:
        path = "input.opus"

    # Ensure no NULs and encode as UTF-8. The fuzzer harness expects a filename string.
    b = path.encode('utf-8')

    # Keep size within 4096 bytes and NUL-terminate to be C-friendly
    b = b[:4095]
    if not b:
        b = b"input.opus"
    if b[-1:] != b"\x00":
        b += b"\x00"
    return b

import random
import struct
import zlib
import base64

# This generator produces a minimal, valid Ogg Opus stream image in memory.
# It builds a simple Ogg bitstream with:
#  - Page 0 (BOS): OpusHead, OpusTags (each packet segmented as needed)
#  - Page 1: small audio packet
#  - Page 2 (EOS): small audio packet marked EOS
# The packets are segmented across the lacing table when >255 bytes. Output <= 4096 bytes.

# Ogg page helpers

def ogg_crc(data: bytes) -> int:
    return zlib.crc32(data) & 0xFFFFFFFF


def segment_packet(pkt: bytes) -> tuple[list[int], bytes]:
    # Split a packet into lacing segments of size 255 (0xFF) followed by a final <255 segment
    segs = []
    body = bytearray()
    i = 0
    n = len(pkt)
    while i < n:
        chunk = min(255, n - i)
        segs.append(chunk)
        body += pkt[i:i + chunk]
        i += chunk
    if n == 0:
        segs.append(0)
    return segs, bytes(body)


def build_ogg_page(serial: int, seqno: int, granule: int, packets: list[bytes], bos: bool, eos: bool) -> bytes:
    seg_table: list[int] = []
    body_parts = []
    for pkt in packets:
        segs, body = segment_packet(pkt)
        seg_table.extend(segs)
        body_parts.append(body)
    body = b"".join(body_parts)
    header = bytearray()
    header += b'OggS'            # capture pattern
    header += b'\x00'           # stream structure version
    hdrtype = 0
    if bos:
        hdrtype |= 0x02
    if eos:
        hdrtype |= 0x04
    header += bytes([hdrtype])   # header type
    header += struct.pack('<Q', granule & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF)  # granule position
    header += struct.pack('<I', serial & 0xFFFFFFFF)           # bitstream serialno
    header += struct.pack('<I', seqno & 0xFFFFFFFF)            # page sequence no
    header += b'\x00\x00\x00\x00'                           # placeholder CRC
    header += bytes([len(seg_table) & 0xFF])                   # page_segments
    header += bytes(seg_table)                                 # segment table
    crc = ogg_crc(bytes(header) + body)
    header[22:26] = struct.pack('<I', crc)
    return bytes(header) + body

# Opus header helpers

def make_opus_head(channel_count: int, mapping_family: int, input_rate: int, pre_skip: int, gain_q8: int) -> bytes:
    # RFC 7845 Section 5.1
    b = bytearray()
    b += b'OpusHead'                   # magic
    b += b'\x01'                       # version
    b += bytes([channel_count & 0xFF])
    b += struct.pack('<H', pre_skip & 0xFFFF)
    b += struct.pack('<I', input_rate & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    # gain_q8 must be a signed 16-bit integer in Q8 dB units
    if gain_q8 < -32768:
        gain_q8 = -32768
    if gain_q8 > 32767:
        gain_q8 = 32767
    b += struct.pack('<h', gain_q8)    # int16 little-endian
    b += bytes([mapping_family & 0xFF])
    if mapping_family == 0:
        # mono or stereo only
        pass
    elif mapping_family == 1:
        stream_cnt = max(1, min(255, channel_count))
        coupled = min(stream_cnt, channel_count // 2)
        b += bytes([stream_cnt & 0xFF])
        b += bytes([coupled & 0xFF])
        b += bytes(range(channel_count))
    else:
        raise ValueError('Unsupported mapping family in generator')
    return bytes(b)


def make_vendor_string(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    vendors = [
        'libopus 1.3.1', 'opusenc 0.2.1', 'GStreamer opus', 'FFmpeg', 'Xiph.Org libopusfile'
    ]
    v = rnd.choice(vendors).encode('utf-8')
    return struct.pack('<I', len(v)) + v


def make_user_comments(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    tags = [
        ('TITLE', ['Test Tone', 'Silence', 'Opus Sample']),
        ('ARTIST', ['Fuzz Bot', 'Opus Project']),
        ('ALBUM', ['Fuzz Suite', 'Sample Pack']),
        ('R128_TRACK_GAIN', ['+3.00 dB', '-5.50 dB', '+0.00 dB']),
        ('R128_ALBUM_GAIN', ['-1.00 dB', '+2.50 dB'])
    ]
    n = rnd.randint(1, 5)
    entries = []
    for _ in range(n):
        t, vals = rnd.choice(tags)
        val = rnd.choice(vals)
        s = f"{t}={val}".encode('utf-8')
        entries.append(struct.pack('<I', len(s)) + s)
    if rnd.random() < 0.3:
        # Tiny 1x1 PNG
        png = (b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"
               b"\x00\x00\x00\rIHDR\x00\x00\x00\x01\x00\x00\x00\x01\x08\x06\x00\x00\x00\x1f\x15\xc4\x89"
               b"\x00\x00\x00\x0cIDATx\x9cc\x00\x01\x00\x00\x05\x00\x01\r\n-\xb4"
               b"\x00\x00\x00\x00IEND\xaeB`\x82")
        b64 = base64.b64encode(png)
        pic = b"METADATA_BLOCK_PICTURE=" + b64
        entries.append(struct.pack('<I', len(pic)) + pic)
    comment_count = struct.pack('<I', len(entries))
    return comment_count + b''.join(entries)


def make_opus_tags(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    b = bytearray()
    b += b'OpusTags'
    b += make_vendor_string(rnd)
    b += make_user_comments(rnd)
    return bytes(b)


def make_small_audio_packet(rnd: random.Random, channels: int) -> bytes:
    # Use Opus CN packet (1 byte 0xFC) which decoders accept as valid.
    return bytes([0xFC])


def build_stream(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    serial = rnd.randrange(1, 2**32 - 1)
    if rnd.random() < 0.7:
        channels = rnd.choice([1, 2])
        mapping_family = 0
    else:
        channels = rnd.choice([3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8])
        mapping_family = 1
    input_rate = rnd.choice([0, 44100, 48000, 96000])
    pre_skip = rnd.choice([0, 80, 312, 3840, 8000])
    gain_q8 = random.choice([0, -256, 256, -1024, 1024])  # already within int16 range

    head = make_opus_head(channels, mapping_family, input_rate, pre_skip, gain_q8)
    tags = make_opus_tags(rnd)

    # Page 0: BOS with OpusHead and OpusTags
    p0 = build_ogg_page(serial=serial, seqno=0, granule=0, packets=[head, tags], bos=True, eos=False)

    # Page 1: audio packet with granulepos = pre_skip
    audio_pkt = make_small_audio_packet(rnd, channels)
    p1 = build_ogg_page(serial=serial, seqno=1, granule=pre_skip, packets=[audio_pkt], bos=False, eos=False)

    # Page 2: EOS with a small packet and advanced granulepos
    audio_pkt2 = make_small_audio_packet(rnd, channels)
    gp2 = pre_skip + 960  # 20 ms advance at 48 kHz
    p2 = build_ogg_page(serial=serial, seqno=2, granule=gp2, packets=[audio_pkt2], bos=False, eos=True)

    return p0 + p1 + p2


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    # Occasionally return an empty buffer to exercise empty-stream path
    if rnd.random() < 0.05:
        return b''
    data = build_stream(rnd)
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data

    query = _rand_query(rng)
    frag = _rand_fragment(rng)
    return f"{scheme}{userinfo}{host}{port}{path}{query}{frag}"

def _build_file(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    root = _rand_choice(rng, _FILE_ROOTS)
    # 0-3 directory segments
    segs = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0,3)):
        seg = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ ") for _ in range(rng.randint(1,10)))
        segs.append(seg)
    leaf = _rand_choice(rng, _FILE_NAMES)
    path = root + "/".join(filter(None, segs + [leaf]))
    # Ensure proper file:// prefix rules: file://localhost/path or file:///path
    if path.startswith('/'):
        url = "file://" + path
    else:
        # Windows absolute like C:/...
        url = "file:///" + path
    return url

def _make_url(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    scheme = _rand_choice(rng, _SCHEMES)
    if scheme == "file://":
        return _build_file(rng)
    else:
        return _build_http_https(rng, scheme)

def _cap_len(url: str, max_tail: int = 256) -> str:
    # The stub concatenates scheme + tail then truncates tail to 256.
    # We supply a full URL directly, but FUZZ_PARAM_STR may read the entire bytes until NUL/newline.
    # Keep each line <= 256 to stay within stub truncation when appended to scheme.
    if len(url) > max_tail:
        return url[:max_tail]
    return url

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    urls: List[str] = []

    # Include a few deterministic edge cases
    urls.append("file:///tmp/test.opus")
    urls.append("http://localhost/stream.opus")
    urls.append("https://example.com/music/track01.opus?q=opus#t=10")

    # Range header style via query to influence server behavior
    urls.append("http://127.0.0.1:8080/audio.opus?range=bytes=0-&mode=preview")

    # Auth info
    urls.append("https://user:pass@example.com/dir/stream.opus")

    # IPv6 host
    urls.append("http://[::1]/index.opus")

    # Windows file path
    urls.append("file:///C:/media/sample.ogg")

    # Unicode filename
    urls.append("file:///home/user/%E9%9F%B3%E6%A5%BD.opus")

    # Randomly generate additional diverse URLs
    for _ in range(20):
        url = _make_url(rng)
        urls.append(url)

    # Cap each to a reasonable length as the stub tail is limited
    urls = [_cap_len(u) for u in urls]

    # Join as lines so FUZZ_PARAM_STR() can pick segments; terminate each with NUL too
    # to accommodate consumers that expect C-strings. Keep total under 4096 bytes.
    out_parts: List[bytes] = []
    total = 0
    for u in urls:
        b = u.encode('utf-8') + b"\0\n"
        if total + len(b) > 4096:
            break
        out_parts.append(b)
        total += len(b)

    return b"".join(out_parts)

import random
import struct
import zlib

# Generates plausible Ogg Opus stream prefixes suitable for op_test/op_*_callbacks initial bytes.
# Focus: valid OggS pages with OpusHead and OpusTags packets, varying fields and sizes.
# Keep under 1024 bytes as stubs truncate to that. We target <= 1000 bytes.

OPUS_HEAD_MAGIC = b"OpusHead"
OPUS_TAGS_MAGIC = b"OpusTags"

# Ogg page helpers

def crc32_ogg(data: bytes) -> int:
    # Ogg CRC32: standard IEEE CRC32 with polynomial 0x04C11DB7, initial 0.
    return zlib.crc32(data) & 0xFFFFFFFF


def build_ogg_page(header_type: int, granule: int, serial: int, pageno: int, segments: list[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # segments: list of complete laced segments concatenated to packets; each element must be <= 255 bytes
    body = b"".join(segments)
    lacing = bytes([len(s) for s in segments])
    header = bytearray()
    header += b"OggS"              # capture pattern
    header += bytes([0])            # version
    header += bytes([header_type & 0xFF])
    header += struct.pack('<q', int(granule))  # granule position (signed 64)
    header += struct.pack('<I', int(serial) & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    header += struct.pack('<I', int(pageno) & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    header += struct.pack('<I', 0)        # CRC placeholder
    header += bytes([len(lacing)])
    header += lacing
    # Compute CRC with CRC field set to 0
    crc_input = bytes(header) + body
    crc = crc32_ogg(crc_input)
    # Patch CRC
    header[22:26] = struct.pack('<I', crc)
    return bytes(header) + body


def cut_into_segments(pkt: bytes, max_seg: int = 255) -> list[bytes]:
    # Cut packet into laced segments of size <= max_seg; for simplicity, split into chunks of up to 255.
    return [pkt[i:i+max_seg] for i in range(0, len(pkt), max_seg)]


def build_opus_id_header(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    version = 1
    # Favor common channel counts but allow 1..8
    channel_choices = [1, 2, 5, 6, 8]
    ch = rng.choice(channel_choices) if rng.random() >= 0.2 else rng.randint(1, 8)
    pre_skip = rng.choice([0, 312, 384, 960, 0])  # include 0 and common pre-skip values
    rate = rng.choice([0, 48000, 44100, 24000])   # original input sample rate (0 allowed per spec)
    gain_q8 = rng.randint(-32768, 32767)          # signed int16 range
    # mapping family selection: mostly 0 for mono/stereo, sometimes 1 for surround
    mapping_family = 0 if (ch <= 2 and rng.random() < 0.85) else 1

    head = bytearray()
    head += OPUS_HEAD_MAGIC
    head += bytes([version & 0xFF])
    head += bytes([ch & 0xFF])
    head += struct.pack('<H', pre_skip & 0xFFFF)
    head += struct.pack('<I', rate & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    head += struct.pack('<h', gain_q8)  # pack as signed short directly
    head += bytes([mapping_family & 0xFF])
    if mapping_family != 0:
        # For family 1 mappings (Vorbis order)
        if ch == 1:
            stream_count, coupled = 1, 0
        elif ch == 2:
            stream_count, coupled = 1, 1
        else:
            coupled = min(ch // 2, 2 if ch >= 6 else ch // 2)
            stream_count = coupled + (ch - 2 * coupled)
        head += bytes([stream_count & 0xFF])
        head += bytes([coupled & 0xFF])
        mapping = list(range(ch))
        head += bytes(mapping)
    return bytes(head)


def build_opus_tags(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build a basic OpusTags packet with vendor and a few comments.
    vendor = rng.choice([
        b"libopus 1.3.1",
        b"opusenc 0.2.1",
        b"GStreamer opus",
        b"FFmpeg"
    ])
    comments = []
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        gain_track = rng.randint(-15000, 15000)
        comments.append(f"R128_TRACK_GAIN={gain_track}".encode('utf-8'))
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        gain_album = rng.randint(-15000, 15000)
        comments.append(f"R128_ALBUM_GAIN={gain_album}".encode('utf-8'))
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        comments.append(b"TITLE=Test Track")
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        comments.append(b"ARTIST=Fuzz Band")
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        comments.append(b"METADATA_BLOCK_PICTURE=")

    blob = bytearray()
    blob += OPUS_TAGS_MAGIC
    blob += struct.pack('<I', len(vendor))
    blob += vendor
    blob += struct.pack('<I', len(comments))
    for c in comments:
        blob += struct.pack('<I', len(c))
        blob += c
    return bytes(blob)


def assemble_stream_prefix(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Construct two Ogg pages: BOS with OpusHead, then a page with OpusTags, optionally audio.
    serial = rng.randrange(1, 0xFFFFFFFF)
    # Page 0: BOS, granule 0, header packet
    id_hdr = build_opus_id_header(rng)
    id_segments = cut_into_segments(id_hdr)
    bos_page = build_ogg_page(header_type=0x02, granule=0, serial=serial, pageno=0, segments=id_segments)

    # Page 1: OpusTags packet. granule 0 for header pages.
    tags = build_opus_tags(rng)
    tag_segments = cut_into_segments(tags)
    tags_page = build_ogg_page(header_type=0x00, granule=0, serial=serial, pageno=1, segments=tag_segments)

    # Optional small audio data page
    add_audio = rng.random() < 0.6
    audio_page = b""
    if add_audio:
        toc = bytes([rng.randrange(0, 256)])
        # generate a few random payload bytes (1..20)
        n = rng.randint(1, 20)
        try:
            payload = rng.randbytes(n)  # Python 3.9+ Random provides randbytes
        except AttributeError:
            payload = bytes(rng.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(n))
        pkt = toc + payload
        segs = cut_into_segments(pkt)
        audio_page = build_ogg_page(header_type=0x00, granule=960, serial=serial, pageno=2, segments=segs)

    data = bos_page + tags_page + audio_page
    if len(data) > 1000:
        data = data[:1000]
    return data


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    mode = rng.random()
    if mode < 0.15:
        return build_opus_id_header(rng)
    elif mode < 0.25:
        return build_opus_tags(rng)
    else:
        return assemble_stream_prefix(rng)
